answers.answer: For 2/3/4 players, deal 4/3/2 starting Player cards each. Remove Epidemic cards and set them aside before shuffling and dealing the remaining City and Event cards. Pawns matching the dealt roles start in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'Remove Epidemic cards and set aside'; starting hands table; 'Place matching colored pawns in Atlanta.'

answers.answer: Put the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2. Reveal 3 Infection cards and put 3 matching cubes on each named city; reveal 3 more and put 2 on each; reveal 3 more and put 1 on each. Put all 9 revealed cards in the Infection Discard Pile; the rest form the Infection Deck. The summary does not explicitly state which end the remaining cards are put at or in what orientation.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 8: 'leftmost 2'; 3/2/1 cubes across three groups; 'Place all 9 flipped cards on the Infection Discard Pile. Remaining Infection cards form the Infection Deck.'

answers.answer: Use 4 Epidemics for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic; remove unused Epidemic cards. Divide the remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles as equal in size as possible, shuffle one Epidemic into each, and stack the piles with smaller piles on the bottom. The summary does not prescribe which pile sizes go where if multiple piles have equal sizes.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7: difficulty counts; 'equal in number ... and as equal in size as possible'; 'Stack the piles ... placing smaller piles on the bottom.'

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions; actions may repeat and the player may stop early. Cards discarded for action costs go to the Player Discard Pile. Then draw 2 Player cards together, resolve Epidemics first, and discard/play Events until within the hand limit; then Infect Cities. After all three phases, play passes to the left.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Actions: 'up to 4'; 'may repeat ... or stop early'; action discards go to Player Discard Pile; phases and pass left.

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry moves to a city connected by a white line and costs no card. Direct Flight discards the City card naming the destination. Charter Flight discards the City card matching the city of departure to move anywhere. Shuttle Flight requires departure from a city with a research station and moves to any other city with a research station; no card cost is stated. White lines going off one board edge wrap to the other edge (example: Sydney and Los Angeles).
answers.evidence: Movement Actions table; Special Rules: 'white lines going off one edge ... wrap to the other edge.'

answers.answer: Normally, spend one action, discard the City card matching your current city, take a station from the supply, and place it in your city. If all six are on the board, relocate one from anywhere on the board. If the box supplied more than six, set extras aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Other Actions: Build a Research Station; Special Rules: 'If more than 6 stations supplied: Set extras aside during setup.'

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action can remove cubes of only one chosen color. If that color is cured, remove all cubes of that color from the city; if it is uncured, remove one cube. To clear the other colors, use separate actions, choosing each color in turn. Removed cubes return to the cube supply.
answers.evidence: Treat Disease: remove 1 cube, or 'all cubes of that one color' if cured; 'Treat each different color with a separate action'; cubes return to supply.

answers.answer: At any research station, discard 5 City cards of the same disease color (4 for the Scientist) and move that disease's cure marker to its Cure Indicator. The station city need not match the disease color. Existing cubes remain, and the cured disease can still receive cubes through infections and Epidemics. If none of its cubes are on the board when cured, it is immediately eradicated and its marker is flipped.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure and Discover a Cure: same-color cards at any station; existing cubes remain; if no cubes, immediately eradicate and flip marker.

answers.answer: Normally, give or take the City card matching the city where both players are located. Both players must agree. If the recipient exceeds 7 cards, they immediately discard or play Event cards until at most 7.
answers.evidence: Share Knowledge: matching current-city card, same city, both agree; recipient exceeding 7 must immediately discard or play an Event.

answers.answer: The Researcher may give any City card from the Researcher's hand to another player in the same city, on either player's turn. The exception does not let another player give an arbitrary nonmatching City card to the Researcher; that transfer still must match the shared city. Both players must agree under the normal Share Knowledge rule.
answers.evidence: Roles—Researcher: any card from Researcher to other player, on either player's turn; no arbitrary nonmatching card to Researcher. Share Knowledge: both players agree.

answers.answer: After the actions, draw the top 2 Player cards together. If fewer than 2 cards remain when the draw is required, the players immediately lose; discards are not reshuffled. The summary does not detail whether any special partial draw is made when exactly one remains.
answers.evidence: Drawing Player Cards: 'Draw the top 2 cards together'; 'If fewer than 2 cards remain ... game ends and the players lose (do not reshuffle discards).'

answers.answer: Resolve Increase, Infect, then Intensify. Increase the Infection Rate marker one space. Draw the bottom Infection card; for a non-eradicated color, add enough cubes to bring that city to 3, and because it already has two, add one more; then an outbreak occurs. Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile. Intensify by reshuffling only that discard pile and placing it on top of the Infection Deck. Do not draw a replacement Epidemic card. The summary does not specify the detailed outbreak spread in this Epidemic subsection, but the outbreak rules say cubes spread to connected cities and chain reactions resolve afterward.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: Increase, Infect, Intensify; 'add only enough to reach 3, then an outbreak occurs'; discard to Infection Discard Pile; no replacement. Outbreaks: spread to connected cities.

answers.answer: After 0 through 6 Epidemics, the Infection cards flipped per turn are respectively 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4.
answers.evidence: Player Reference, Infection Rate Track table: Epidemics resolved 0-6 gives 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4.

answers.answer: Resolve all three steps of the first Epidemic, then all three steps of the second; Events may be played between them. After drawing, resolve all Epidemics before enforcing the 7-card hand limit. The summary says an Event cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card, but may be played between the two Epidemics.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: 'resolve all 3 steps for the first, then all 3 steps for the second. Events may be played between the two'; Hand Limit: after drawing, first resolve all Epidemics, then enforce limit.

answers.answer: Flip cards from the top of the Infection Deck, one at a time, equal to the current infection rate. For a normal non-eradicated disease, add one matching cube to the named city, unless it already has three, in which case an outbreak occurs instead of a fourth cube. For an eradicated disease, place no cube. A cured but non-eradicated disease can still infect and receive cubes. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities: top of Infection Deck; one per card; eradicated means no placement; 3 cubes causes outbreak; cured disease can still infect; discard each card.

answers.answer: The first outbreak advances the Outbreaks marker once and spreads one cube to every connected city. If a connected city already has three cubes of that color, it outbreaks after the current outbreak resolves, advancing the marker again and spreading to its connected cities. Do not add cubes to cities that already had an outbreak during this Infection card, so the spread does not return into the first city if it already outbreaked. Each color has its own cap of three cubes per city; multiple colors may coexist.
answers.evidence: Outbreaks: marker forward; spread to every connected city; chain reaction after current outbreak; skip cities already outbreaked; 'up to 3 of each.'

answers.answer: No. Airlift cannot be played between drawing an Infection card and resolving it, so it cannot move the Quarantine Specialist after the triggering card is drawn but before its outbreak. An Event may be played after resolving that card and before drawing the next one; any player may play it, and the player playing it chooses its use. It costs no action and the played Event goes to the Player Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: any player, at any time, not an action; cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card; player decides use; discard to Player Discard Pile.

answers.answer: As an action, the Contingency Planner takes one Event card from anywhere in the Player Discard Pile and stores it on the Role card. Capacity is one, and it does not count toward the hand limit. When played, remove it from the game instead of discarding it.
answers.evidence: Roles—Contingency Planner: 'As an action'; 'from anywhere'; limit 1; doesn't count against hand limit; remove from game when played.

answers.answer: As an action, the Dispatcher may move any pawn to a city with another pawn, or move another player's pawn as if their own; the owner's agreement is required when moving another player's pawn. Direct/Charter Flight costs come from the Dispatcher's hand. For a Charter Flight, the card matches the moved pawn's departure city. The Dispatcher may not direct another pawn to Treat Disease or take other nonmovement actions, and cannot use the Operations Expert's special move.
answers.evidence: Roles—Dispatcher: both options, owner's agreement; movement only when directing; flight discards from Dispatcher hand and Charter card matches moved pawn's departure; cannot use Operations Expert special move.

answers.answer: Players win immediately when cures for all four diseases are discovered; eradication and a clear board are not required. They lose if the Outbreaks marker reaches the last space (the 8th outbreak), if required cubes cannot be placed because the supply for a color is exhausted (loss immediately during an Epidemic, outbreak, or infection), or if a player cannot draw two Player cards after their actions.
answers.evidence: Victory and Defeat: cures for all four; diseases need not be eradicated; three loss triggers; Special Rules says cube-supply failure is immediate.

answers.answer: Place the board within reach, with six research stations and disease cubes separated by color nearby; place one station in Atlanta; put the Outbreaks marker at 0 and the four cure markers vial-side up near their indicators. Give each player a Reference card; shuffle Role cards and deal one face up to each, placing matching pawns in Atlanta; remove unused Role cards and pawns. The first player is the one with the highest-population City card. The summary does not say whether the board supply includes any additional setup handling beyond the six stations and separated cubes.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1-5 and 9 specify supplies, Atlanta station, markers, role/reference dealing, unused pieces, and highest-population City card.

answers.answer: The active player decides their own actions if teammates disagree; teammates may offer advice. Introductory hands are face up for all to see. Standard and Heroic hands are private by default, though experienced groups may choose open hands. Anyone may inspect either discard pile at any time.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'player whose turn it is decides'; Special Rules: Introductory face up; Standard/Heroic private by default, experienced groups may choose open; anyone may examine either discard pile.

answers.answer: Removing the last cube before that disease is cured does not eradicate it and has no effect. Removing the last cube after it is cured eradicates it; flip the cure marker to the eradication side. Once eradicated, the disease gets no new cubes during normal infections or Epidemics.
answers.evidence: Eradication: uncured last cube has no effect; last cube of cured disease flips marker; eradicated diseases receive no new cubes during infections or Epidemics.

answers.answer: Place 3 cubes of that color in the city. Reaching exactly three does not itself cause an outbreak; the outbreak rule triggers when a city already has three and a further cube would be placed. Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile before Intensify reshuffles that pile onto the top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: place 3; 'If the city already has cubes ... add only enough to reach 3, then an outbreak occurs'; discard to discard pile; Intensify reshuffles it on top.

answers.answer: Increase still occurs. The eradicated color gets no cubes. The Infection card is still discarded to the Infection Discard Pile, then Intensify still reshuffles only that pile onto the top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards gives Increase/Infect/Intensify sequence; Infect says 3 cubes unless eradicated and discard the card; Infecting Cities says eradicated diseases get no cubes.

answers.answer: After the first Epidemic, its Infection discard pile is intensified and emptied. The second Epidemic's bottom Infection card is then the only card in the discard pile, so the second Intensify shuffles that card onto the top of the Infection Deck. It is drawn first in normal Infections and, under the stated conditions, normally causes an outbreak when its city is already at three cubes after the second Epidemic placed three. The question stipulates zero cubes initially in the second Epidemic city; the Epidemic adds three. The summary notes this normally causes an outbreak unless an Event, eradication, or role protection prevents it.
answers.evidence: Two Epidemics: after first Intensify discard pile empty; second bottom card alone is shuffled, ends on top and drawn first; normally causing an outbreak absent protections.

answers.answer: The Scientist needs 4 same-color City cards rather than 5 for Discover a Cure. The cure still requires a research station; the station city's color need not match the disease color.
answers.evidence: Scientist role: needs only 4 same-color City cards; Cure Procedure: at any research station; station city color need not match.

answers.answer: As an action, the Operations Expert builds a research station in their current city without needing to hold, use, or discard a City card.
answers.evidence: Operations Expert: 'As an action: build a research station in the current city with no City card needed, used or discarded.'

answers.answer: Once per turn, as an action, the Operations Expert may move from a city with a research station to any city by discarding any City card. The card need not match the origin or destination. The summary does not state any additional restriction on destination beyond 'any city.'
answers.evidence: Operations Expert: 'Once per turn as an action: move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card.'

answers.answer: A Medic's Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one chosen color from the Medic's city, even if that disease is uncured. It does not remove cubes of multiple colors in one action; each color would require another action.
answers.evidence: Medic: Treat Disease removes all cubes of one color; Treat Disease says each different color takes a separate action.

answers.answer: When the cure is discovered while the Medic is already in a city with cubes of that color, the summary does not explicitly state that discovery itself triggers automatic removal. It says the Medic automatically removes all cubes of a cured disease from any city entered or occupied, with no action needed, and that it works on other players' turns if moved by Dispatcher or Airlift. Thus, it supports removal on a later move into another such city, without an action; timing for the Medic already occupying a city when the cure is discovered is unsupported by the summary.
answers.evidence: Medic role: automatically removes all cubes of cured diseases from any city entered or occupied; no action needed; works on others' turns if moved by Dispatcher or Airlift.

answers.answer: The Medic prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in the Medic's city. This does not protect adjacent cities or uncured diseases.
answers.evidence: Medic role states these location, disease, and adjacency limits.

answers.answer: The Quarantine Specialist protects their current city and every city connected to it from cube placement and outbreaks of every disease color. The ability does not affect cubes placed during setup.
answers.evidence: Quarantine Specialist role: every color, current and connected cities; no effect on setup cubes.

answers.answer: Resilient Population removes any one card from the Infection Discard Pile from the game. It may be played between the Epidemic Infect and Intensify steps, so it can remove the card just discarded during that Epidemic before the discard pile is reshuffled.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: remove any one card in Infection Discard Pile from game; may be played between Infect and Intensify.

answers.answer: One Quiet Night skips the next Infect Cities step and no Infection cards are flipped for that skipped step. It does not skip the Infect step of an Epidemic.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: One Quiet Night skips next Infect Cities step, do not flip Infection cards; does not skip Epidemic Infect.

answers.answer: Airlift moves any one pawn to any city. If it is another player's pawn, get that player's permission.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Airlift effect.

answers.answer: Only Player cards count toward the 7-card limit. Role and Reference cards do not count, and the Contingency Planner's stored Event does not count. If a hand has nine counted cards, discard cards or play Event cards until the player has at most seven; the summary does not prescribe which two cards must be removed.
answers.evidence: Hand Limit: Player cards only; Role and Reference do not count; discard/play Events until at most 7. Contingency Planner storage does not count against hand limit.

answers.answer: Government Grant places a research station in any city, regardless of the player's location, without discarding a City card.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Government Grant: place a research station in any city, no card discard needed.

answers.answer: Forecast lets the player draw, view, and rearrange the top 6 cards of the Infection Deck, then put them back on top of that deck.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Forecast effect.
